dish: Momiji no tempura (salt-aged maple leaves fried in sweet batter)
n: Hisakuni Kōsendō (久國紅仙堂, Minoo momiji tempura)
w: Frying Minoo's signature momiji no tempura since 1940 a minute from Hankyu Minoo Station at the foot of the falls trail, using maples grown on its own hillside; featured by Time Out Japan and Rurubu.

dish: Momiji no tempura (fried maple leaves), fried fresh on the trail
w: Atlas Obscura credits Momotaro, opened in 1901 on the trail to Minoo Falls, as the shop that started selling fried maple leaves; Rurubu's Minoo foliage feature cites its original recipe.

address: Takatsuki–Ibaraki area (Tabelog area 高槻), Osaka Prefecture
w: Niboshi-broth specialist open since 2011 in the northeast corner of Osaka; selected for Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025 (a repeat selectee) and reviewed by Ramen Adventures.

dish: Clear-broth (seiyu) ramen and rich chicken-pork 'potage' ramen
n: Saishiki Ramen Kinsei Takatsuki Honten (彩色ラーメンきんせい 高槻本店)
w: Takatsuki flagship of the Kinsei group, with two signature lines, a refined clear broth and a thick chicken-pork potage; Tabelog Ramen OSAKA Hyakumeiten 2025, and eaten and logged by Ramen Adventures.

n: Le Sucré-Coeur Kishibe (ル・シュクレクール 岸部)
w: The 2004 boulangerie that reshaped Japan's bread scene, by a France-trained baker; the original Kishibe shop was revived in 2020. On Time Out's 23 must-go restaurants in Northern Osaka and profiled by All About's bread guide.

dish: Sobameshi (chopped yakisoba fried with rice in sauce)
n: Okonomiyaki Aomori (お好み焼 青森, Shin-Nagata)
w: The Nagata okonomiyaki shop (opened 1957, now third generation) credited as the birthplace of sobameshi, first made when factory workers asked for their cold rice to be fried with yakisoba; featured by FEEL KOBE and traced in Kobe Shimbun's Nagata konamon series.
